title: Reproducible and scalable differentiation of highly pure cortical neurons from human induced pluripotent stem cells
protocol: Prepare required number of iPSCs on vitronectin-coated 6-well plates as described above.
Prepare required number of GTX-coated wells of a 12-well plate; coat two to three wells of a 12-well plate per well of a 6-well plate of iPSCs.
Clean off spontaneously differentiated cells in the iPSC culture thoroughly before starting neural induction.
Split iPSCs into wells of a GTX-coated 12-well plate when they reach 70%–80% confluence; define this day as Day-in-vitro 0 (DIV0).
Add 0.5 mL Accutase to the well with iPSCs and incubate for 5-8 minutes at 37°C until most cells detach.
Monitor under a microscope that cells are detaching before proceeding further.
Gently triturate detached cells with DMEM-F12 using a P1000 pipette, count cells, and transfer the required amount of cell suspension (1 million cells per well) into a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin the cell suspension for 4 minutes at 170 g at room temperature.
Aspirate media from the cell pellet and resuspend in NI supplemented with RI to achieve a single-cell solution at 1 million cells/mL.
Plate 1 mL of cell suspension (1 million cells) per well on GTX-coated plates, resulting in a cell density of 260,000 cells/cm².
Evenly distribute the cells by moving the plate back and forth in two directions.
Increase plating density if cells are not confluent the next day.
Decrease plating density if issues with detaching cells occur later.
Change NI media every day until DIV7.
Feed 1 mL NI per well of a 12-well plate for the first days.
Increase media volume to 1.5–2 mL on DIV5-7 to ensure sufficient supply with growth factors and nutrients.
Use E6-NI gradient for difficult-to-differentiate cell lines on DIV0 and DIV1 starting with the split.
On DIV0, perform split using 1 mL E6-NI gradient medium-1 instead of NI.
On DIV1, change medium to 1 mL of E6-NI gradient medium-2.
On DIV2, change medium to NI and continue with the standard protocol.
Coat wells of a 6-well plate with 1 mL of each PO and L as described under materials and equipment.
Aspirate coating solution completely from the coated wells on DIV7.
Leave the plate open in the laminar flow hood to dry for about 20–30 minutes, turning around once after 10–15 minutes to allow even drying.
Aspirate the medium from the cells.
Add 0.5 mL of Accutase to the cells.
Incubate for 10 minutes at 37°C.
Add 1 mL of DMEM-F12 to wash off the cells, obtaining a single cell suspension.
Pool the cell suspension in a 15 mL conical tube and count the cells.
Spin down the cells.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in an appropriate amount of NI/RI to achieve a concentration of 30 million cells per mL.
Place one drop of 250–350 μL cell suspension per well on dried POL 6-well plates.
Ensure the cell suspension stays in the middle of each well without dispersing and avoid introducing air bubbles.
If necessary, gently tilt and tap the plate to spread the spot slightly so its diameter is about 1/3 to 1/2 of the well diameter.
Let the cells attach for 60 minutes at room temperature without adding additional media.
Place the lid on the plate and keep it inside the hood during attachment.
Add 2 mL NI/RI very gently to the wall of the plate with a serological pipette.
Tilt the plate very gently to spread out the NI.
Ensure that cells stay in the spot and are not washed off.
Shake or tap the plate to dislodge any non-attached/dead cells the next day.
Replace the medium with fresh 2 mL NI.
Change NI media every day, using 3–4 mL feeds to bridge one weekend day.
Switch to 2 mL NM media on DIV10.
For subsequent feeds starting from DIV10, change NM media every day, using 3–4 mL feeds to bridge one weekend day.
Check the quality of cells in the 12-well plate before making spots.
Ensure cells are in a uniform layer without peeling off or dying.
Optimize starting cell density if necessary for more proliferative iPSC lines.
Shift the day of making spots to DIV6 for confluent but stable cell layers.
Dry POL-coated plates until an even crystalline sheet appears on the bottom.
Ensure gaps do not exist in the crystalline sheet to prevent spot peeling.
Maintain integrity of neural rosettes during expansion.
Feed cells with 2 mL NM supplemented with bFGF (20 ng/mL) when neural rosettes appear around DIV15 for two consecutive days.
Change NM media daily, using 3–4 mL feeds to bridge weekend days as culture progresses.
Split cells with NRSR when rosettes start accumulating around DIV20–23.
Manually select neural rosettes inside the spot after splitting to increase purity and enrich for NPCs.
Split spots in a 3:2 to 3:4 ratio onto POL-coated 6-well plates.
Aspirate media from the plates.
Add 1 mL NRSR and incubate for 30–60 minutes at 37°C.
Aspirate NRSR and add 1.5 mL NM.
Manually isolate rosettes from inside the spot using a pipette tip.
Collect dislodged rosettes in a 15 mL conical tube, triturate slightly with a Pasteur pipette or P1000 to break up larger clumps.
Spin down cells and remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells carefully in NM + bFGF, triturate 1–2 times with a 5 mL serological pipette.
Plate 2 mL of the cell suspension per well of a POL-coated 6-well plate.
Feed rosettes with NM + bFGF on the next day.
Change NM media (without bFGF) every day to every other day for subsequent feeds.
Split cultures containing single rosettes and small aggregates when they become almost confluent, usually around DIV30–33.
Incubate with 0.5 mL Accutase for 4 minutes at 37°C without aspirating.
Add 1 mL NM after the incubation period.
Wash cells off with a plastic Pasteur pipette or P1000 pipette.
Pool and triturate gently with a Pasteur pipette or P1000 to separate rosettes from each other, avoiding single cell formation.
Spin down the collected cells and resuspend in fresh NM + bFGF.
Plate cells in 2 mL of NM + bFGF per well of a 6-well plate.
Feed cultures with NM + bFGF on the next day.
For subsequent feeds, feed with NM media every day to every other day.
Add 0.5 mL Accutase to the cells.
Incubate for 4 minutes at 37°C.
Do not aspirate Accutase, add 1 mL NM and triturate cells gently with Pasteur pipette without breaking up rosettes.
Collect cells in a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin down cells and resuspend NPCs in 1 mL cold Freeze Medium for Neural Rosettes for every 1–2 collected wells, depending on cell density; tritrate 2–3× with 5 mL pipette.
Transfer cell suspension to cryovials and freeze vials with 1 mL cell suspension in prechilled Mr. Frosty at -80°C.
Save a drop to genotype cells if needed.
Transfer frozen rosettes to liquid nitrogen tank for long-term storage.
Count cells before freezing by triturating a small, representative aliquot to single cells.
Freeze NPCs at about 10 million cells per cryovial.
Document yield and/or quality of the cells after differentiation.
Coat required number of wells/plates with POL the day before thawing.
Prepare 9 mL Neurobasal media in 15 mL conical tubes, one tube per vial thawed.
Prepare Thawing Medium for Neural Rosettes, use 2 mL per vial thawed if plating in a 6-well plate.
Quickly thaw frozen rosettes in a 37°C water bath until only a small clump of ice remains.
Add 0.5 mL of prepared Neurobasal media into the cryovial to dilute freeze medium.
Pipette the rosettes up and down 1–2 times with Pasteur pipette if no large clumps are present, or with P1000 pipette if large clumps are present.
Gently transfer the thawed cell suspension to the prepared tubes with Neurobasal media.
Spin down cells.
Aspirate supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 2 mL Thawing Medium for Neural Rosettes using a Pasteur pipette.
Plate resuspended cells into one well of a 6-well plate.
Shake the plate to distribute the cells evenly.
Transfer the plate to an incubator.
On day post-thaw (DPT) 1, if the media is yellow, add 1–2 mL fresh NM + bFGF on top.
On DPT 2, perform a full feed with 2 mL NM + bFGF.
Feed the cells 2 mL NM as needed on following days.
On DPT 4–7, split the neurons for long-term culture as described below.
Plate rosettes on DPT 4-7 onto POL-coated plates for stable culture up to 12 months.
Split rosettes onto 6/12/24-well, POL-coated plates at DIV41–47 with cell densities of 160,000–210,000 cells/cm².
Plate 300-400k cells/well in a 24-well plate.
Plate 0.6-0.8 million cells/well in a 12-well plate.
Plate 1.5-2.0 million cells/well in a 6-well plate.
Prepare POL-coated wells/plates as required.
Prepare one 15 ml tube with 4 ml NM per well of a 6-well plate with rosettes.
Prepare required amounts of Accutase (0.5 ml per well of a 6-well plate with rosettes).
Aspirate NM from the wells.
Add 0.5 ml Accutase to rosettes and incubate for 6-10 minutes at 37°C.
Check under microscope that neurons are detached and neurites are retracted.
Increase incubation time if necessary.
Incubation complete, add 1 ml of NM to Accutase with a P1000 pipette.
Triturate 8-12 times with P1000 while holding the plate at a 45° angle and moving the tip left and right to break up remaining rosettes.
Collect cells in a prepared 15 ml tube containing 4 ml of NM.
Transfer single cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer into the prepared 15 mL tube.
Pre-wet the cell strainer and the wall of the 15 mL tube with medium to minimize cell loss and death.
Count cells from one well, which can contain 5–20 million cells depending on density.
Transfer the required number of cells into a new tube.
Spin down the cells in the new tube.
Aspirate the supernatant from the cells.
Resuspend and gently triturate the cells with P1000 pipette in 1 mL Plating medium until no clumps are visible (usually 4–6 times).
Add required media volume to reach recommended cell density.
Plate quickly, occasionally mix the tube when plating many wells.
Triturate cells carefully to avoid introducing air bubbles.
Add cells directly into media if possible.
Tap the plate to dislodge debris and dead cells into the supernatant before feeding the neurons.
Feed the neurons with NB+/B27+ medium supplemented with 10 μM DAPT on day 3 after plating.
Prepare half-feed by supplementing NB+/B27+ medium with 10 μM DAPT and 5 μM 5-Fluorouracil (5FU) and 5 μM Uridine (pre-mixed as 5FU).
Perform half-feeds two to three times per week for a total of 7 days with NB+/B27+ medium supplemented with DAPT.
Continue half-feeds with NB+/B27+ medium supplemented with 10 μM DAPT and 5 μM 5-Fluorouracil (5FU) for 10–14 days after the initial feed on day 3.
If significant cell death occurs during 5FU treatment, perform a full feed by removing all media and replacing it with fresh NB+/B27+ medium supplemented with DAPT and 5FU.
Ensure that media volumes remain constant during half-feeds by briefly tilting plates to check individual well contents after removing media.
Switch to half feeds with NB+/B27+ two to three times per week once the 5FU treatment ends.
